Manaschmiede help
Getting started

Start: double-click Commander-DB starten.bat (or run python commander_db_vNN.py serve in the command prompt, where NN is the version number). A black window opens. Keep it open while you use the database. The browser opens the page automatically (otherwise enter http://localhost:8000).

On a phone: Manaschmiede detects mobile phones and switches to the phone view: navigation as a bar at the bottom (Home, New here?, Deck, Duel, Table, ☰ More), a compact header with 📱 view, 🎨 style and ❓ help, and full-width fields. The view button (📱/🖥 top right) switches between “automatic”, “always phone” and “always PC”, which helps on tablets.
At startup the program checks in the background for new rules, precons or card data. The bar at the top shows the progress. You can already work in the meantime.

Continue editing a saved deck: choose it at the top of the “Build deck” tab under “📂 Open saved deck”, or click it on the welcome page under “Last saved”. Manage decks (versions, sharing, deleting) in the “My decks” tab.
A first deck: on the welcome page (or in the “Build deck” tab under “Commander”) type a name (e.g. “Atraxa”), click a suggestion and press Suggest deck. A complete 100-card deck appears below.
Quit: close the black window (or press Ctrl+C in it). Saved decks are kept.

Page layout: the page starts with the welcome page: type a commander there and press “Build deck”, or click one of the cards. The tabs at the top lead to all areas: Build deck (assistant and deck view), Opponents & duel (comparison, combos, Forge), My decks (import, saved decks), Collection, Game table, Card search and Rules. The browser's back button jumps to the previous tab.
All over the page you'll find small ? buttons. Clicking one opens the matching section of this help. At the top right you can switch the style between Magic style and neutral.
What is Commander? (in one minute)

Every deck has exactly 100 cards, one of which is the commander, usually a legendary creature. It sits in the command zone instead of the library and can be cast from there at any time (each additional time it costs 2 more mana).
Each card may appear only once. Basic lands such as Forest or Island are the exception.
The commander's color identity determines which colors are allowed in the deck. A green-blue commander only allows green, blue and colorless cards.
Everyone starts with 40 life. A player who has taken a total of 21 combat damage from a single commander also loses.
Precons are the ready-made, officially sold Commander decks and make a good benchmark.
Brackets (levels 1–5) describe how strong a deck is, so that decks of similar strength play against each other.
Let the assistant build a deck (deck-building assistant)
All fields are optional; one entry is enough.

Commander: suggestions appear as you type; typos are tolerated. The color identity is taken over automatically. Separate two commanders (partner, background) with “ + ”, e.g. “Thrasios, Triton Hero + Tymna the Weaver”.
Theme: e.g. mill, lifegain, tokens, Voltron. The deck is built around this theme.

No commander yet? Click your favorite colors with the color buttons (W U B R G ◇) and/or enter a theme, in English or German, e.g. “dragons”, “elves”, “tokens”, “graveyard”, “artifacts”, “lifegain”, including enchantment and artifact types such as “sagas”, “auras” or “equipment”. “💡 Suggest commanders” shows twelve matching commanders with image, reasoning and rules text. Each time you get a new mix of ⭐ popular commanders, 💎 hidden gems (played less often) and 💶 budget options, from different color combinations if the colors are open. Commanders whose text explicitly supports the theme are listed first as “exact match”. “🔄 Other suggestions” shows more commanders not shown yet; “🔀 Reshuffle” starts over. Normally the colors must match exactly; “also with fewer colors” additionally shows commanders with only some of the colors. “No Game Changers” and “Max price per card” apply here too. “✔ Take this commander” applies it. If a deck is suggested without a commander, the suggestions appear automatically.
Color identity: only needed if you don't enter a commander (W = white, U = blue, B = black, R = red, G = green).
Cards that should go into the deck: your own favorite cards, one per line. Add them with the field above and Enter.
No Game Changers: leaves out especially strong cards; useful for casual games.
Max price per card / total budget: no card above the max price, or the whole deck (excluding basic lands) stays within the budget. Cards without a known price are then not suggested.
Unavailable cards: cards you don't own or don't want to play. They are never suggested; the browser remembers the list.

First the assistant picks cards that fit the commander's text (e.g. counters, tokens, lifegain or its creature types). This group is called “Synergy with the commander”. The rest is based on general popularity (EDHREC). With several colors, lands that produce two or more of the deck's colors are preferred. The result is a starting point; the fine-tuning is up to you.
View and adjust the deck
View: “List” (compact, with prices and links) or “Card images”.
⇄ Swap: shows suitable alternatives with the same role (e.g. other ramp). Filters: no Game Changers, max price. Optionally the old card is remembered as “unavailable”.

➕ Add card: type a name and pick a suggestion. The card is checked (Commander-legal, matching color identity, not a duplicate) and filed under “Added manually”. Basic lands can be added multiple times.
✕ Remove, + / − on basic lands: takes a card out or changes the number of a basic land. The deck header then shows how many cards are missing or too many.
🏷 Tags: your own categories per card (e.g. Ramp, Wincon). They appear as labels in the list and are grouped in the “By tags” section.
↓ Maybe / maybeboard: candidates that don't count towards the deck (yet). “↑ to deck” brings them back; the field above takes new candidates.
Tokens and game pieces: lists all tokens created by cards in the deck, together with the card that creates them.

🖨 Print proxies: print view at original size (63 × 88 mm, 9 per page, A4 or Letter). You'll find it in the deck, in the collection under “Proxy printing” for any card list, and in the buying assistant. Choose card images or an ink-saving text version, back faces of double-faced cards, tokens, only missing cards, or a specific printing via “(SET) No.”. Copies for private testing only: not real cards, do not sell them or pass them off as real, not allowed in tournaments; every copy carries the fixed mark “PROXY – not a real card”. “Print / save as PDF” creates a PDF file; when printing, choose 100 % or “Actual size”. The official card back is not printed. Tip: put the cut-out copy into a sleeve together with a real, worthless card (e.g. a basic land), copy facing front. Then all cards look the same from behind, even in clear sleeves.

💡 Recommendations, gaps and filters: under “Gaps by function” the program counts ramp, card draw, targeted removal and board wipes and compares them with guideline values (about 10 / 10 / 8 / 3). If something is missing, six suitable, widely played cards in your colors are listed for each function (➕ adds them). “only from my collection” shows only cards you own; “at most … € per card” sets a price limit (your own cards count as free). In server mode, the published gallery decks of other users are included as well.

💡 Recommendations: looks for similar decks (precons, your saved decks and, in server mode, the gallery, with at least three shared cards) and suggests cards that are often played there together with your cards or that fit the commander's text. “Consider cutting” names cards with little backing; cards tagged 🏷 “Wincon” or “Combo” are never suggested. Decks with a good win rate in the game log count more.

Frustration index: our own estimate from the card text of how much a deck can annoy other players (mass land destruction, extra turns, stax, theft, counterspells, tutors, Game Changers). It replaces EDHREC's salt scores, for which there is no official interface.
Price history: at every card data update (once a day at startup) changed prices are recorded. The deck shows its value over time and the cards with the biggest changes over the last 30 days.
Notes / primer: free text about the deck. Tags, maybeboard and notes are saved with the deck and restored when it is loaded.
Replace all Game Changers: swaps all of them at once for the best alternative.
Mana curve: how many cards have which cost. Many cheap cards = fast deck.
Prices are euro guideline values from the Cardmarket price list (trend price of the cheapest printing), otherwise from the Scryfall data.

Mana base: counts the sources per color (lands including fetch and search lands, mana artifacts/creatures up to mana value 2; ramp spells up to mana value 3 that fetch a land count as half) and calculates how likely you can cast each card on time. “Too few sources” means: plan more lands or mana of that color. The hardest cards are on the right.

Sample hand: draws 7 random cards; “Draw a card” simulates the next turns, “Mulligan” reshuffles (London mulligan). Above it are statistics from 20,000 opening hands: how often the hand is keepable (2–5 lands) and how often you can play a land on turns 1–4.

Deck editor: “↶ Undo” / “↷ Redo” (also Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) revert any change to the list (60 steps). Custom groups: drag a card into another group (while dragging, a bar with all groups, the maybeboard and “Remove” appears at the bottom) or tap ⇄ on the card and pick a group or create a new one. Custom groups are saved with the deck, shown as sections on the share page and passed on as categories in the Archidekt export. “☐ Multi-select” puts checkboxes in front of the cards; the marked cards can be moved, tagged, put in the maybeboard or removed together. The “Stacks” view shows the cards as image stacks by mana value; tapping one finds a replacement.

🎮 Test board: plays through the deck alone, turn by turn (goldfishing): keep the opening hand or mulligan (the first one is free), then draw, play lands and spells, cast your commander (tax +2 per cast). The table is laid out like digital card games: the opponent at the top (life, library, face-down hand), the battlefield in the middle (creatures and co. towards the center, lands towards the edge, identical lands stacked), your hand as a fan at the bottom. At the bottom left your avatar with life total, next to it 📚 library, 🪦 graveyard, 🌀 exile and the command zone; at the bottom right the big “End turn” button (Space) and 🃏 to draw. At the top the phase bar (tapping marks the phase; tapping the current one = continue). Controls: tapping a card shows only the fitting actions (e.g. “Play”, “Tap”, “Cast”), “More” the rest; cards can also be dragged: onto the battlefield, 🪦, 🌀, 📚, the hand or the command zone. Tapping twice taps the card, a long press or right-click enlarges it. Tap the avatar: life, poison, commander damage. Everything else is behind ⚙: playmat (deck colors, felt, parchment, commander image), text view “Aa”, card size, landscape, tokens from the deck, dice and coin, statistics, log, end game. Short messages show what just happened; ↶ undoes steps (key Z). The table does not enforce the rules.
Import and save
Save: in the framed “💾 Save deck” box directly below the deck heading, enter a name and click Save. Same name = the old deck is overwritten.
Saved decks are in the collapsible section “Import deck & saved decks”, with the buttons “My deck” (load), “Opponent” (use as opponent), “Versions” and “Delete” (click twice).

Share: creates a link to a read-only page of the saved deck (with images, tags, notes). “Revoke link” invalidates it immediately. In local mode the link only works on the PC or in your home network; in server mode, on the internet.

📤 Send: in server mode you pick another user and optionally a message; the deck lands in their inbox (“📥 Received decks” at the top of My decks, with a counter on the menu item) and is saved there as their own deck with “Apply” (with “(from …)” if the name already exists) or declined. Without user accounts (locally or in the home network), “Send” creates a link with a QR code, which you send e.g. by messenger via “Send via …”. The other person pastes the link into the link field of their Manaschmiede under “Import deck”; the whole deck is copied over. The link works as long as your Manaschmiede is reachable for the other person.

Versions: every time you save a deck with a changed list, the previous version is kept (up to 30). Under “Versions” you see what has been added or removed since then and can restore an old version. The current one is also kept as a version. When saving you can add a note on the change; in the versions window you can compare any two versions.

German card names: lists, collections and the card search also understand German (and other non-English) names, e.g. “Blitzschlag” → Lightning Bolt. Unknown names are looked up once on Scryfall and then remembered; this needs an internet connection.

Import: paste a list (e.g. from Moxfield “Export”), choose a file (.txt, .dck, .dec, .csv, .json) or enter a link (Archidekt, MTGGoldfish, TappedOut, Deckstats; Moxfield often blocks links, then copying the list helps). Files are recognized in any common character encoding, including MTGO (.dek) and Cockatrice (.cod). Then click Import.

The preview shows whether the commander was recognized, which cards were not found or were corrected, and whether anything is outside the color identity. You can change the commander there; separate partners with “ + ”.
Precons: ready-made Commander decks

The “🎁 Precons” section shows all official Commander precons (preconstructed decks by Wizards of the Coast) with their full decklists, sorted by set and release date. The lists come from the freely available collection github.com/taw/magic-preconstructed-decks-data (also the basis of mtg.wtf and MTGJSON) and are updated automatically along with the other data.

Search by deck name, commander or set; the color buttons only show decks with at most these colors. Each deck shows its value (sum of the single cards, excluding basic lands), a bracket estimate and, if you have set up a collection, how much of it you already own.

Tap a deck to open its list. “✏ Open in deck editor” loads it for adjusting (analysis, test board, upgrades); “💾 Save to My decks” creates your own copy; “⚔ As opponent” sets it for comparison and Forge duels; “📥 Bought: add to my collection” adds all its cards to your collection (after a confirmation).
Collector's editions with an identical list appear only once. Cards missing from the card database (e.g. brand-new promo cards) are named with the deck.
Brackets: the official power levels

With the Commander Brackets (by Wizards of the Coast and the Commander Format Panel, officially still “beta”) you agree before the game how strong your decks are, so that decks of similar strength play each other. They help with that conversation and don't ban any cards.
Bracket
What to expect
Deck-building rules
1 Exhibition
Theme or idea before power, hardly optimized; games last at least about 9 turns.
no Game Changers, no mass land destruction, no extra turns, no two-card combos
2 Core
Unoptimized and straightforward, wins come gradually and can be disrupted; relaxed and social; at least about 8 turns.
no Game Changers, no mass land destruction, no intentional two-card combos, only a few extra turns and not in a row
3 Upgraded
Strengthened with good synergy and card quality, can disrupt opponents; the win can come in one big turn; at least about 6 turns.
at most 3 Game Changers, no mass land destruction, no chains of extra turns, no two-card combos that win before about turn 6
4 Optimized
Lethal, consistent and fast, but not aimed at the tournament metagame; at least about 4 turns.
only the ban list
5 cEDH
Built for the competitive metagame; games can end on any turn.

Game Changers: an official list of especially powerful cards (currently 53, as of February 9, 2026, e.g. Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Demonic Tutor). They are not banned but determine the bracket. The marking comes with the Scryfall card data and is up to date after every update.
Mass land destruction / mana denial: cards like Armageddon or “lands don't untap”. They are not intended for brackets 1–3.
Extra turns: a few are fine from bracket 2, “chains” (several in a row or in a loop) only from bracket 4. The program counts more than 3 extra-turn cards as a chain.

Two-card combos: two cards that win the game together (e.g. infinite damage). Bracket 3 only allows them if they don't come together before about turn 6. Manaschmiede checks this automatically via Commander Spellbook as soon as a deck is loaded (needs internet; without a connection this point stays open and can be checked later with “🔗 Check combos again”). The earliest turn is an estimate from many drawn sample hands.

How Manaschmiede rates decks: in the deck view, “🎚 Bracket rating” shows for each rule what was found and, from that, the lowest possible bracket. What a program can't see stays open: whether a deck without restricted cards is bracket 1 or 2 (intent), and whether a strong deck is 4 or 5 (tournament metagame). That's why you set your target bracket yourself; it is saved with the deck and shown as “B3” in “My decks”, in the gallery (also as a filter) and on the share page. Without a target, the estimate “≈B3” is shown there. If the deck contains cards above the chosen target, ⚠ appears with the cards concerned.
At the table: announce your bracket and mention anything special (combos, extra turns, strong commanders). The official status is published by Wizards: introduction, latest update (Feb 9, 2026).
Deck gallery (server mode only)

Publish: under “📂 My decks”, tap “🌍 Publish” on the deck. The deck then appears in the gallery for all logged-in users of this server; tapping again withdraws it. Changes to the deck are applied when you save.
Search: by commander, deck name, user, tags and notes; color filter (at most/exactly/at least these colors), max price, Game Changers; sorted by new, popular or budget.

Open a deck: view the list, notes and maybeboard, “♡” to like, “📥 Copy to my decks” (the original stays unchanged), “⚔ As opponent” and write comments. You can delete your own comments and comments on your own deck.
Administrator: can remove decks from the gallery with “🚫 Hide” and delete any comment.
My collection

Import: in the “My collection” section, choose a CSV file from ManaBox, Moxfield, Deckbox, Archidekt or Dragon Shield, or paste a list. “Add” adds the cards to the existing collection, “Replace” starts over. Unrecognized names are shown.

Ownership: each deck shows what percentage you own and what is missing (with price). In the list, ✓ marks cards you own, ✗ missing ones, and ⚠ cards that are already in another saved deck and of which not enough copies are free.
Building from your collection: in the assistant choose “Collection: prefer” (own cards first) or “own cards only”. Basic lands always count as owned.

📷 Scan cards: in the “Collection” tab (or in the deck view next to “Add”). Three ways: Take photo (works everywhere; on a phone the camera opens), Live camera (in the browser only via HTTPS or on the PC) and, in the Android app, “Scan with phone camera” (recognition directly on the device, especially fast). Set the card language and capture the card straight and filling the frame. The name is recognized; if uncertain, alternatives are offered. Continuous scan: in the live camera, “🔁 Start continuous scan” (or in the Android app “Continuous scan with phone camera”), then place the cards in the frame one after another; every reliably recognized card is added to the scan list automatically with a sound. The same card only counts again after it has briefly left the picture; for several identical copies tap “+1”. With single scans, add each card to the scan list with “✓ Apply”, adjust quantities with + / −, and finally “Add to collection” or “To current deck”. The very first scan loads the text recognition once (about 25 MB, internet needed); after that it works without. For very large collections, specialized scanner apps (ManaBox, Delver Lens) are faster, and their CSV can still be imported.

🛒 Shopping list: counts all cards you are missing for your saved decks, with price and deck assignment. “Cards move between decks” (default) counts the largest quantity in any one deck; otherwise each deck gets its own copies. The list can be copied (the “1 Card name” per line format is also understood by the Cardmarket wishlist) or put entirely on your own wishlist.

⭐ Wishlist and price alert: cards with quantity and an optional target price. If the current price is below it, the card is marked green in the list and shown as “🔔 Price alert” on the start page. Cards from your collection whose price has changed by at least 20 % and €1 within about seven days also appear there. New prices come with every card data update.
📁 Folders: organize parts of the collection (e.g. trade binder, binder). A folder only holds cards you own, and at most as many as you have; the cards remain part of the collection.

🛒 Seller links: each card has small links straight to the seller: CM Cardmarket (cheapest printing) and TO Trader-online (search for the card). For precons, CC cardcosmos is added, which only sells sealed products. “🛒 Buy on Cardmarket” in the shopping list and wishlist copies the whole list and opens Cardmarket's Wants page: create a new list, “Add decklist”, paste. The Shopping Wizard then finds the cheapest combination of sellers. Login and purchase always happen directly with the seller; Manaschmiede transmits no data. Below the shopping list, each seller can be switched off.

📚 Stock by printing: each row is one printing of your card with set, collector number, finish (normal, foil, etched), condition (Cardmarket grades MT, NM, EX, GD, LP, PL, PO), language and quantity. Everything can be changed directly in the table; ✎ opens the list of all printings of the card with image and price (normal and foil). Entries with identical details are merged; quantity 0 removes the entry. Above the table, “Choose printing …” adds a card in a specific printing. On import, set, number, foil, condition and language are taken over from ManaBox, Moxfield, Deckbox, Archidekt and Dragon Shield, and from text lists like “2 Counterspell (MH2) 267 *F*”. The program fetches the printing data (set name, image, Cardmarket ID) from Scryfall; if Scryfall is unreachable, the details are kept and can be completed later with “Load printing data”. Value: the Cardmarket price of exactly this printing (foil with the foil price), otherwise the Scryfall price of the printing; without a known printing, the card's cheapest printing counts. Condition and language don't change the value because the Cardmarket price list doesn't distinguish them. Deck building, ownership, shopping list and folders use the total per card. The “Download as CSV” export contains all printing details and can be read back in (also by Moxfield, ManaBox, Archidekt).

🧭 Buying assistant: plans buying missing cards for one deck, all decks or the wishlist. With a budget, cards used in several decks are planned first, then the cheapest; whatever doesn't fit is marked. For each card you choose printing and foil, the seller (Cardmarket or Trader-online) or “don't buy”. For Cardmarket, the assistant copies the cards with any printing for the Wants list; you add fixed printings and foils to the cart via the product links. The precon check shows precons that contain several of the missing cards. Tick the cards you bought and add them “as bought to the collection”; the wishlist is shortened accordingly.
🖨 Proxy printing: prints copies of any card list for private testing; see “Print proxies” under “View and adjust the deck”.
📈 Value history: the value of the collection per snapshot date (at every card data update), with the dollar value for comparison.

Price sources and budget swap: euro prices come straight from the public Cardmarket price list, which is reloaded every day. A card's price is the trend price of its cheapest printing, i.e. roughly what you pay for a playable copy. Clicking the price in the card search also shows the lowest price, the 1-, 7- and 30-day averages, the foil price and the number of printings; 🛒 opens the cheapest printing on Cardmarket. If the price list is unreachable, the most recently loaded Cardmarket prices apply, and without any price list, Scryfall's euro prices. Dollar prices (TCGplayer) come from Scryfall. In the deck view, “💸 Budget swap” finds replacements with the same role for expensive cards (from an adjustable price, excluding your own cards) at no more than 30 % of the price; one click swaps the card.
Game table: life counter and game log
Start a game: choose the number of players (2–6) and starting life, enter names and pick a saved deck for each player or type one freely.
